resources.description: Explicit CPU and memory configuration for each Redis replica. When omitted, the preset defined in `resourcesPreset` is applied.

resourcesPreset.description: Default sizing preset used when `resources` is omitted.

size.description: Persistent Volume Claim size available for application data.

storageClass.description: StorageClass used to store the data.

external.description: Enable external access from outside the cluster. Can be enabled only when the instance is created, together with `tls.enabled: true`; turning it on for an existing instance, or changing `tls.enabled` while it is on, is refused at admission.

tls.description: TLS configuration. TLS is opt-in and is not inferred from `external`.

authClients.description: Maps to the Redis `tls-auth-clients` directive. Defaults to `no` — the server certificate is presented but client certificates are not validated. `yes` requires a client certificate signed by this release's CA, which the platform does not issue. Changing it restarts the Redis and Sentinel pods, because the directive is read from the config file once at startup.

enabled.description: Enable TLS for Redis and Sentinel connections. Disabled unless set. Enabling it moves Redis and Sentinel to a TLS-only listener, so existing plaintext clients must be migrated at the same time. Encryption is provided by the redis-operator fork that mounts the certificate Secret into both Redis and Sentinel pods at `/tls`.

minReplicasToWrite.description: Redis `min-replicas-to-write`: the master refuses writes unless at least this many replicas are connected and within `minReplicasMaxLag`. Unset by default, which leaves the Redis default (disabled). With `replicas: 2` and a value of 1 the master rejects writes while its only replica is down, trading availability for a bound on the writes lost if an isolated master is failed over. Replication stays asynchronous, so this bounds the loss, it does not remove it. Must be 0 or more and below `replicas` (a master with `replicas` pods has `replicas - 1` replicas), otherwise every write is refused; the chart refuses such a value.

minReplicasMaxLag.description: Redis `min-replicas-max-lag`, in seconds: a replica whose last acknowledgement is older than this does not count towards `minReplicasToWrite`. Unset by default, which leaves the Redis default (10). Has no effect unless `minReplicasToWrite` is set. Must be at least 1 when `minReplicasToWrite` is set: Redis treats 0 as disabling the check, so the chart refuses it.
